# zgetc2

> Computes an LU factorization with complete pivoting of a general N-by-N complex matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zgetc2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgetc2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zgetc2( order, N, A, LDA, IPIV, strideIPIV, JPIV, strideJPIV ) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · N-by-N complex matrix (overwritten with L and U) |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of A |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Row pivot indices (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride for IPIV |
| `JPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Column pivot indices (length N) |
| ↳ `strideJPIV` | `integer` | Stride for JPIV |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the n-by-n matrix to be factored. On exit, the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U \, Q$; the unit diagonal elements of L are not stored. If U(k, k) appears to be less than SMIN, U(k, k) is given the value of SMIN, giving a nonsingular perturbed system.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le N$, row i of the matrix has been interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.
- `JPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le j \le N$, column j of the matrix has been interchanged with column `JPIV(j)`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if U(info,info) is small

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zgetc2.strided(
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    JPIV, strideJPIV, offsetJPIV
) → info: integer
```

Computes an LU factorization with complete pivoting of a general N-by-N complex matrix.

The factorization has the form `A = P * L * U * Q`, where P and Q are
permutation matrices, L is lower triangular with unit diagonal elements,
and U is upper triangular.

IPIV and JPIV are 0-based in this implementation.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · N-by-N complex matrix (overwritten with L and U) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A (in complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Row pivot indices (length N), 0-based |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for IPIV |
| `JPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Column pivot indices (length N), 0-based |
| ↳ `strideJPIV` | `integer` | Stride for JPIV |
| ↳ `offsetJPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for JPIV |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the n-by-n matrix to be factored. On exit, the factors L and U from the factorization $A = P \, L \, U \, Q$; the unit diagonal elements of L are not stored. If U(k, k) appears to be less than SMIN, U(k, k) is given the value of SMIN, giving a nonsingular perturbed system.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le N$, row i of the matrix has been interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.
- `JPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le j \le N$, column j of the matrix has been interchanged with column `JPIV(j)`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if U(info,info) is small

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = k`, U(k, k) is likely to produce overflow if one tries to solve for x in $\mathrm{Ax} = b$. So U is perturbed to avoid the overflow.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zgetc2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgetc2';

// 3x3 complex matrix (real-only entries) in column-major order:
const N = 3;
const A = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const view = reinterpret( A, 0 );
view[ 0 ] = 4.0; view[ 2 ] = 1.0; view[ 4 ] = 2.0; // column 0
view[ 6 ] = 1.0; view[ 8 ] = 5.0; view[ 10 ] = 1.0; // column 1
view[ 12 ] = 2.0; view[ 14 ] = 1.0; view[ 16 ] = 6.0; // column 2

const IPIV = new Int32Array( N );
const JPIV = new Int32Array( N );

const info = zgetc2( 'column-major', N, A, N, IPIV, 1, JPIV, 1 );
console.log( 'info =', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'IPIV =', IPIV ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'JPIV =', JPIV ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGETC2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGETC2 computes an LU factorization, using complete pivoting, of the n-by-n matrix A. The factorization has the form $A = P \, L \, U \, Q$, where P and Q are permutation matrices, L is lower triangular with unit diagonal elements and U is upper triangular.

This is a level 1 BLAS version of the algorithm.

</section>
